chapterNote: An alphabet of rescue, written out of David's least dignified deliverance — the day he drooled in his beard and scratched at the gate of Gath, feigning madness before Abimelech until the Philistine king drove him out (1 Samuel 21). No angel of glory that day, only an escape that looked like disgrace; and out of it David builds an acrostic, one line per Hebrew letter, teaching the whole alphabet of the fear of the LORD. The psalm moves from testimony — I sought, He answered; this poor man cried, He heard; taste and see that the LORD is good — to a school-room: come, children, and learn what the good life is made of, a guarded tongue, a turn from evil, peace pursued. The theology beneath it is honest about pain: many are the afflictions of the righteous, hearts do break, spirits are crushed — and there, precisely there, the LORD is near. Not one bone broken became literal at the cross (John 19:36), and 'taste and see' became Peter's invitation to the newborn church (1 Peter 2:3): the psalm of the fugitive turned out to be about the Redeemer, and no one who takes refuge in Him will bear the guilt.

1.text: Of David, when he changed his behavior before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed. I will bless the LORD at every moment; His praise will be in my mouth continually.
1.amp: A Psalm of David, when he changed [shanah] his behaviour [taam — his taste, his sanity's appearance] before [panim] Abimelech ['or, Achish', the KJV margin]; who drove him away [garash], and he departed [yalak]. I will bless [barak] the LORD [YHWH] at all times [et]: His praise [tehillah] shall continually [tamid] be in my mouth [peh].
1.notes: The superscription is the scandal: taam (H2940) is 'taste, judgment' — David scrambled his own appearance of sanity at Gath (cf. 1 Samuel 21:13) and was garash (H1644), driven out like a beggar. From THAT rescue comes 'at ALL times': tamid (H8548), the word for the perpetual temple offerings — praise as a standing sacrifice, humiliations included.

2.text: My soul will make her boast in the LORD; the humble will hear of it and be glad.
2.amp: My soul [nephesh] shall make her boast [halal] in the LORD [YHWH]: the humble [anav — the lowly, the afflicted] shall hear [shama] and be glad [samach].
2.notes: halal (H1984), to boast: the one legitimate bragging (cf. Jeremiah 9:24). The anavim (H6035) are glad at another's rescue because every deliverance of one lowly man is a promissory note to all the rest.

3.text: O magnify the LORD with me, and let us lift His name high together.
3.amp: O magnify [gadal — make great, declare great] the LORD [YHWH] with me, and let us exalt [rum] His name [shem] together [yachad].
3.notes: gadal (H1431): not making God bigger but making His greatness visible, as a lens magnifies. yachad (H3162), together — testimony refuses to stay solo; the rescued man immediately recruits a choir.

4.text: I went seeking the LORD, and He answered me, and He tore me free from all my fears.
4.amp: I sought [darash] the LORD [YHWH], and He heard [anah — answered] me, and delivered [natsal — snatched away] me from all my fears [megurah — terrors].
4.notes: darash (H1875) is deliberate seeking, and the deliverance reaches past the dangers to the megurah (H4035), the fears themselves — God rescues not only from Gath but from the terror Gath planted in the chest.

5.text: Those who look to Him are radiant, and their faces will never be covered with shame.
5.amp: They looked [nabat] unto Him, and were lightened [nahar — made radiant, as with flowing light]: and their faces [panim] were not ashamed [chapher].
5.notes: nahar (H5102) doubles as 'to flow' and 'to shine' (the KJV margin keeps both): faces turned toward God catch light like water catches dawn. The shame-word chapher (H2659) is what the fugitive at Gath had every reason to expect and never received.

6.text: This poor man cried, the LORD heard, and out of all his troubles He saved him.
6.amp: This poor man [ani] cried [qara], and the LORD [YHWH] heard [shama] him, and saved [yasha] him out of all his troubles [tsarah].
6.notes: 'This ani (H6041)' — David points at himself, the drooling beggar of the superscription. The whole gospel of the psalm in one line: cried, heard, saved — qara, shama, yasha (H7121, H8085, H3467), the shortest supply chain in the world.

7.text: The Angel of the LORD encamps all around those who fear Him, and He delivers them.
7.amp: The angel [malak] of the LORD [YHWH] encamps [chanah] round about them that fear [yare] Him, and delivers [chalats — draws them out, arms them] them.
7.notes: One malak YHWH (H4397) makes a surrounding machaneh, a whole camp — the same figure who met Joshua as commander of the LORD's host (cf. Joshua 5:14; 2 Kings 6:17). chalats (H2502) is both to rescue and to equip for war: the guarded become the armed.

8.text: O taste and see that the LORD is good; oh the blessedness of the man who takes refuge in Him!
8.amp: O taste [taam] and see [raah] that the LORD [YHWH] is good [tov]: blessed [esher] is the man [geber — the strong man] that trusts [chasah — takes refuge, shelters] in Him.
8.notes: The taste-verb (H2938) shares its root with verse 1's taam: the 'taste' David faked at Gath becomes the real tasting of God's goodness — firsthand experience, not hearsay. chasah (H2620) is refuge-taking, and Peter serves this verse to every newborn believer (cf. 1 Peter 2:3).

9.text: O fear the LORD, you His holy ones, for the ones who fear Him want for nothing.
9.amp: O fear [yare] the LORD [YHWH], ye His saints [qadosh — His holy ones]: for there is no want [machsor — lack] to them that fear Him.
9.notes: The qadoshim (H6918), the set-apart ones, are commanded the yirah that protects them. 'No machsor' (H4270) is Psalm 23:1 in other words — the fear of the LORD and the shepherding of the LORD produce the same balance sheet.

10.text: Young lions go hungry and lack, but those who seek the LORD will not lack any good thing.
10.amp: The young lions [kephir] do lack [rush — go destitute], and suffer hunger [raeb]: but they that seek [darash] the LORD [YHWH] shall not want [chaser — lack] any good [tov] thing.
10.notes: The kephir (H3715), the lion in its prime — nature's best-equipped hunter — still knows famine, while the seeker's pantry is stocked by covenant. The promise is measured exactly: not everything, but no tov thing (cf. Psalm 84:11).

11.text: Come here, children, and listen to me; the fear of the LORD is what I will teach you.
11.amp: Come [yalak], ye children [ben], hearken [shama] unto me: I will teach [lamad] you the fear [yirah] of the LORD [YHWH].
11.notes: The psalm turns schoolroom: lamad (H3925), to train, and the yirah (H3374) of the LORD as the curriculum — wisdom's beginning (cf. Proverbs 9:10) taught by a man who learned it as a fugitive, not a professor.

12.text: Which of you is the man who desires life, who loves long days in which he may see good?
12.amp: What man [ish] is he that desires [chaphets] life [chay], and loves [ahab] many days [yom], that he may see [raah] good [tov]?
12.notes: The recruiting question every soul answers yes to. Peter quotes verses 12-16 whole as the church's ethics (cf. 1 Peter 3:10-12): the good life has entrance requirements, and they start at the mouth.

13.text: Guard your tongue from evil, and keep your lips from speaking deceit.
13.amp: Keep [natsar — guard as a watchman] your tongue [lashon] from evil [ra], and your lips [saphah] from speaking [dabar] guile [mirmah — deceit, fraud].
13.notes: natsar (H5341) posts a sentry on the lashon (H3956): the first discipline of the good life is verbal. mirmah (H4820) is fraud — and the superscription's own ruse hovers here; the man who once survived by deception teaches its renunciation.

14.text: Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace, and go after it in pursuit.
14.amp: Depart [sur — turn aside] from evil [ra], and do [asah] good [tov]; seek [baqash] peace [shalom], and pursue [radaph — chase, hunt down] it.
14.notes: Four verbs, two negative and two positive: sur, asah, baqash, radaph. The last is the striking one — radaph (H7291) is the word for hot pursuit of an enemy: shalom (H7965) runs, and the righteous man chases it down.

15.text: The eyes of the LORD watch over the righteous, and His ears are turned toward their cry.
15.amp: The eyes [ayin] of the LORD [YHWH] are upon the righteous [tsaddiq], and His ears [ozen] are open unto their cry [shavah].
15.notes: Divine attention as anatomy: ayin (H5869) and ozen (H241), eyes and ears both aimed at the tsaddiq. Verse 6's 'the LORD heard' is here made standing policy.

16.text: But the face of the LORD is set against those who do evil, to cut off every memory of them from the earth.
16.amp: The face [panim] of the LORD [YHWH] is against them that do [asah] evil [ra], to cut off [karath] the remembrance [zeker] of them from the earth [eretz].
16.notes: The same panim (H6440) that lights the faces of verse 5 turns as a wall against evildoers. karath (H3772) is the cutting-word of covenants — here cutting off the zeker (H2143), the memory itself: evil's final future is being forgotten.

17.text: The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears, and He delivers them out of all their troubles.
17.amp: The righteous cry [tsaaq — cry out for help], and the LORD [YHWH] hears [shama], and delivers [natsal] them out of all their troubles [tsarah].
17.notes: The cycle of verse 6 promised to every tsaddiq: tsaaq, shama, natsal (H6817, H8085, H5337). 'All their tsarah' (H6869) — the deliverance is total in scope even when staged in time.

18.text: The LORD is near to the broken-hearted, and He saves those whose spirit is crushed to dust.
18.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is nigh [qarov] unto them that are of a broken [shabar — shattered] heart [leb]; and saves [yasha] such as be of a contrite [dakka — crushed to powder] spirit [ruach].
18.notes: The psalm's deepest verse: qarov (H7138), near — nearest precisely where life has shattered (shabar, H7665) the leb and ground the ruach to dakka (H1793), dust-fine. God's address among men is the broken heart (cf. Isaiah 57:15; Psalm 51:17).

19.text: The afflictions of the righteous are many, but out of them all the LORD delivers him.
19.amp: Many [rav] are the afflictions [ra] of the righteous [tsaddiq]: but the LORD [YHWH] delivers [natsal] him out of them all.
19.notes: No prosperity-promise, but something sturdier: the afflictions are rav (H7227), many, conceded up front — and the deliverance count matches the affliction count exactly. 'Out of them ALL' is the arithmetic of the empty tomb.

20.text: He keeps guard over all his bones; not one of them is broken.
20.amp: He keeps [shamar — guards] all his bones [etsem]: not one [echad] of them is broken [shabar].
20.notes: shamar (H8104), the watchman-verb, posted over every etsem (H6106). At Golgotha the soldiers broke the legs of both thieves and left the Righteous One's bones whole — John cites this line as fulfilled Scripture (cf. John 19:33, 36; Psalm 22:17).

21.text: Evil will put the wicked to death, and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.
21.amp: Evil [ra] shall slay [muth] the wicked [rasha]: and they that hate [sane] the righteous [tsaddiq] shall be desolate ['guilty', asham, the KJV margin].
21.notes: Evil needs no executioner beyond itself: ra (H7451) is subject of the verb, slaying its own practitioners. asham (H816) is guilt with its penalty attached — the sentence hatred of the righteous writes against itself.

22.text: The LORD redeems the soul of His servants, and none of those who take refuge in Him will bear the guilt.
22.amp: The LORD [YHWH] redeems [padah — ransoms] the soul [nephesh] of His servants [ebed]: and none of them that trust [chasah — take refuge] in Him shall be desolate ['guilty', asham, the KJV margin].
22.notes: The acrostic's extra line, added past the alphabet's end to say the one thing more: padah (H6299), ransom-redemption, price paid and nephesh bought back. The psalm's last word reverses verse 21's — lo yeshamu, NOT guilty — for everyone sheltering (chasah, H2620) in Him (cf. Romans 8:1).
